description:
TUTORING CHECKPOINT (one-step Socratic style per .claude/skills/tutor). Goal: teach the author rhoPimpleFoam's pressure-based algorithm from first principles, feeding (a) a new appendix section 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' and (b) understanding of op-26w Part 2 (compressibility psi = drho/dp|_h, why frozen isothermal kappa_T ~100x too small in the dome causes the plateau OVERSHOOT).

WHERE WE PAUSED: just wrote the continuous compressible momentum equation d(rho u)/dt + div(rho u u) = -grad(p) + div(mu grad u), labelled 4 terms (time, convection, pressure, viscous). Paused at the anchor question: identify the 3 'transport skeleton' terms (time+convection+viscous -> a_P, a_N, old-time) vs the 1 odd-one-out source (pressure).

NEXT STEPS (in order): (1) discretise momentum term-by-term into a_P u_P = H(u) - grad(p); (2) rearrange -> u_P = HbyA - rAU grad(p), with rAU=1/a_P, HbyA=H(u)/a_P (the code term that confused the author); (3) substitute the face velocity/flux into discrete continuity to BUILD the pressure equation (this closes the 'pressure is the orphan, continuity pins it' thread); (4) return to Part 2: compressibility psi and the plateau overshoot.

ALREADY COVERED & SOLID: Part 1 energy conservation fully derived by author (conservative vs non-conservative ddt differ by h*r; r=discrete continuity residual; rho_cont=rho_old-(dt/V)sum(phi.A) forces r=0). Author also patched the results-section discrete continuity eqn (added V_cell and face area vectors). FV diffusion stencil (rod example, a_P=a_E+a_W, Fick 2nd law) understood.

APPENDIX NOTE: 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' is textbook -- cite Jasak thesis, Ferziger & Peric, OpenFOAM programmer's guide; present as re-derived established background, NOT original, to keep novelty claims on the solver fixes.
title: Resume tutoring: rhoPimpleFoam momentum discretisation -> a_P u_P = H - grad(p) -> HbyA -> pressure equation

description:
One of the three HTGR-specific accident sequences, none of which had a bead before 2026-08-11. Source material is already in the archive: kugeler2017vhtr (EUR 28712 EN, open) covers modular-HTR safety and its appendix summarises the key safety experiments.

THE PHYSICS. If the primary boundary fails and air enters a hot graphite core, graphite oxidises: C + O2 -> CO2 and the Boudouard reaction C + CO2 -> 2CO, which is endothermic and becomes significant at high temperature. The consequences that matter are structural degradation of the graphite (it is the core structural material AND the moderator), a chemical heat source, and CO production. Reaction rate is diffusion-limited or chemically-limited depending on temperature, so the regime matters more than the raw Arrhenius constant.

WHY THIS IS TRACTABLE HERE. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs already carries the reactor and equilibrium machinery this needs, with zero todo!(): gibbs_reactor.rs (multiphase Gibbs energy minimisation), equilibrium_reactor.rs, conversion_reactor.rs, pfr.rs, cstr.rs, plus a full reactions model. Graphite oxidation is a gas-solid equilibrium-plus-kinetics problem of exactly the shape that layer already solves. Reuse it rather than writing fresh chemistry.

Depends on graphite properties (op-jyyp.1) for the solid side and on the bed model for where the heat goes.

Kinetics must come from open published sources with provenance per DATA_POLICY.md. If only a lumped rate is used, say so in the doc comment rather than implying a mechanistic model.
title: HTR-10 accident: air ingress and graphite oxidation
